name: Windows Service Persistence (sc create / binPath hijack)
description: Creating a Windows service gives SYSTEM-level, reboot-surviving persistence: sc create or New-Service registers a service whose binPath is the payload and which auto-starts as LocalSystem. Alternatively, an existing service's ImagePath/binPath is hijacked (sc config binpath=) to run attacker code. Service control events make this noisy but it remains a classic, reliable SYSTEM persistence and privilege path.
source: MITRE ATT&CK T1543.003; Microsoft service documentation
notes:
=== CREATE A NEW SERVICE (admin; runs as SYSTEM) ===
  sc create <name> binPath= "C:\Windows\Temp\payload.exe" start= auto
  sc description <name> "Windows Update Helper"
  sc start <name>
  # NOTE the required SPACE after each '=' in sc.exe syntax.

  # PowerShell equivalent:
  New-Service -Name <name> -BinaryPathName "C:\Windows\Temp\payload.exe" -StartupType Automatic

=== SERVICE BINPATH HIJACK (existing service) ===
  sc config <name> binPath= "C:\Windows\Temp\payload.exe"
  sc config <name> start= auto
  # abuses weak service ACLs; see weak-service-acl-binpath for the privesc angle.

=== NON-EXE PAYLOADS ===
  A service expects a service-control binary; a plain EXE/one-liner may run then exit (SCM timeout).
  Use a service-aware wrapper (e.g. msfvenom exe-service) or cmd /c start for a non-service payload.

=== ENUMERATE (hunt / verify) ===
  sc query type= service state= all
  Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Where StartMode -eq 'Auto' | Select Name,PathName,StartName

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  Scheduled task (also SYSTEM, quieter), Run keys (user), WMI subscription.

examples.label: Hijack an existing service binPath (weak ACL)
Hunt auto-start services with suspicious paths (defender)
examples.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Where PathName -match 'Temp|AppData|ProgramData' | Select Name,PathName,StartName

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1543.003 - Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service

recommended.note: Run keys are a user-level persistence alternative.
Scheduled tasks give similar SYSTEM persistence more quietly.
Unquoted service paths are a related service-based abuse.

defense.why_it_works: The Service Control Manager runs registered services, by default as LocalSystem, at boot. Creating a service or repointing an existing service's binary is a documented administrative action, so an attacker with admin (or write access to a service's configuration) gains SYSTEM execution that persists across reboots.
defense.prerequisites: Local administrator to create a service or modify HKLM service config; or write access to a specific service's ACL for a targeted binPath hijack. The payload should be service-aware or wrapped.
defense.impact: T1543.003 Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service. Persistent SYSTEM-level code execution surviving reboot; a binPath hijack of an auto-start service also provides privilege escalation.
defense.detection: High-fidelity events exist: System log 7045 (new service installed) and 7040 (start type changed); Security 4697 (service installed, with auditing); Sysmon EID 13 on HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\*\ImagePath. Alert on ImagePath in user-writable/temp paths, cmd/powershell binPaths, and services.exe spawning interpreters.
defense.artifacts: System EID 7045/7040; Security 4697; Sysmon EID 13 on ...\Services\<name>\ImagePath; Security 4688 / Sysmon EID 1 with ParentImage services.exe; the service binary on disk.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog (EventCode=7045 OR EventCode=4697)
| search (ImagePath="*\\Temp\\*" OR ImagePath="*\\AppData\\*" OR ImagePath="*powershell*" OR ImagePath="*cmd.exe*" OR Service_File_Name="*powershell*")
| table _time, Computer, Account_Name, Service_Name, ImagePath, Service_File_Name, Service_Start_Type
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:("7045" or "4697") and winlog.event_data.ImagePath:(*\\Temp\\* or *\\AppData\\* or *powershell* or *cmd.exe*)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "ServiceInstalled"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\","powershell","cmd.exe","-enc")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, AdditionalFields
defense.prevention: Audit service creation (4697/7045) centrally and alert on new or modified services, especially with temp/user-path or interpreter binPaths; harden service ACLs so non-admins cannot reconfigure services (fix weak binPath permissions); restrict local admin; use WDAC/ASR so even a service cannot launch unsigned code; baseline the legitimate service inventory.

detections.name: New service installed with suspicious ImagePath (7045)
detections.logic:
index=wineventlog EventCode=7045 (ImagePath="*\\Temp\\*" OR ImagePath="*\\AppData\\*" OR ImagePath="*powershell*" OR ImagePath="*cmd.exe*" OR ImagePath="*\\ProgramData\\*")
| table _time, Computer, Service_Name, ImagePath, Service_Start_Type
detections.false_positives: Some legitimate installers create services from temp during setup
detections.tuning: Allowlist known installer-created services; correlate with signed binaries

detections.name: services.exe spawning a command interpreter
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "services.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Rare legitimate service wrappers that shell out
